$comment: Bilingual documentation pairs, and the claims that must stay true on both sides.
The app's localisation has two gates (`npm run i18n:gate`, `npm run i18n:audit`) and
the type system on top of them, because a key added to one locale column and not the
other is a `typecheck` failure. The DOCS had neither. docs/README.cs.md and README.md
drifted for months on the one claim a reader most needs to be right: the English side
said a self-hosted install now boots without Firestore or Google OAuth, the Czech side
still said self-hosting `zatím nefunguje`. An agent reading the stale side gets
confidently wrong context and plans around a constraint that no longer exists.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: a translation checker. These two files are not sentence-for-sentence
editions — README.md is the open-source entry point, docs/README.cs.md is the Czech
product overview, and they are allowed to differ in what they cover. What they may not
do is contradict each other on a SHARED FACT. So each rule below names one such fact
twice, once per language, and the check fails when either side stops stating it or when
the two state different values.
DIRECTION: `source` is authored first and `derived` is transcreated from it, matching
the app's own direction since 2026-08-05 (en authors, cs follows — docs/i18n/contract.md).
The derived file carries `marker` in its own header so a reader knows which side wins.
WHEN IT GOES RED. Two shapes, and they want different fixes:
• the DERIVED side stopped matching → the Czech edition fell behind. Update it.
• the SOURCE side stopped matching → the English was reworded or the fact changed.
Re-read the Czech, make it say the same thing, then update this entry's pattern.
Never delete a rule to make the build green: the rule going red IS the drift being
caught, and this is exactly the class of gate ADR-0007 says must be able to fail.
`source`/`derived` are JavaScript regular expressions matched against the file after
normalisation (CRLF dropped, blockquote markers stripped, all whitespace collapsed to
single spaces), so a pattern may span what is a line wrap in the file. When both sides
capture group 1, the captured values must be equal — that is how a version number can
drift on one side only and still be caught.
Run by `npm run docs:parity`, blocking inside `npm run check:ci`.

rules.why: The minimum Node is the first thing a new reader acts on, and `node:sqlite` moved it once already.
The licence is the one claim a reader may rely on legally. It may not differ by language.
The claim that actually drifted. The Czech edition said self-hosting did not work for months after the English said it boots without Firestore or Google OAuth.
rules.source: \*\*Status: partially there\.\*\* A self-hosted production install now boots and runs without Firestore or Google OAuth
rules.derived: \*\*Stav: zatím částečně\.\*\* Self-hosted produkční instalace dnes nabíhá a běží bez Firestore i bez Google OAuth

rules.why: AGENTS.md and the product both promise channel support is 'stated exactly'. Understating Sklik in one language is the same lie as overstating it in the other.
rules.source: \*\*Sklik\*\* has ad-limit checks and keyword suggestions \(plus read-only stats sync with a token\)
rules.derived: \*\*Sklik\*\* má kontroly limitů inzerátů, návrhy klíčových slov a read-only synchronizaci statistik

rules.why: Every public demo number is labelled as belonging to a fictional client. Both editions must name the same one.
The BYOM vendor list is what a self-hoster checks before deciding they can run this for free.
rules.source: six vendors: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Qwen and Ollama
rules.derived: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / OpenRouter / Qwen / Ollama

rules.why: A security property stated to users. Stating it differently in one language is worse than not stating it.
The two-minute start is the only instruction most readers follow. Both editions must give the same commands.
As above — the command that actually boots the offline product.
